before: Adjacent vertical margins of ordinary block siblings can collapse. With two positive margins, the gap is the larger one, not their sum.

The class selectors match the two blocks. margin-bottom: 24px and margin-top: 16px set their touching vertical margins. display: flow-root on the outer box contains its contents, but does not prevent these sibling margins collapsing. after: Collapsing margins means two margins join into one gap. This can happen between ordinary blocks stacked vertically. When both margins are positive, the gap uses the larger value instead of adding them.

The first block’s bottom margin meets the second block’s top margin. They collapse because this is ordinary block layout. `flow-root` keeps the group’s layout separate from its surroundings, but does not stop these sibling margins from collapsing.
If the first margin becomes 8 pixels, the second margin is now larger. The resulting gap would be 16 pixels. In this example, compare the two positive values and take the larger one.

This lesson uses horizontal writing and ordinary block siblings. Flex and grid item margins do not collapse this way. Negative margins also need different arithmetic. Do not apply the larger-value rule to every kind of spacing.
Set the first bottom margin to 24 pixels and the second top margin to 16 pixels. Inspect the gap in the preview. It should be 24 pixels, not 40.
